ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In an experiment, a solid 1 molar sample of Substance A was gradually heated by a source of constant energy for several hours and the temperature was measured periodically. At the end of the heating period, Substance A had been converted to the gas phase. The heating curve produced by this experiment is shown below. During the course of the experiment, there was a period of time when the phase of Substance A was in equilibrium with the liquid phase. At what temperature did this occur?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a heating curve of temperature changing with time, with the vertical axis as Temperature (K) and the horizontal axis as Time (hours). The curve rises from about 100 K to 150 K, then a horizontal plateau appears at 150 K; afterward the temperature continues to rise to about 250 K, another longer horizontal plateau appears at 250 K, and finally it continues to rise. Reasoning: The sample is initially a solid, and after continuous heating it finally becomes a gas. The horizontal plateaus in the heating curve represent phase-change processes, during which two phases are at equilibrium. The first horizontal plateau encountered after the solid is heated corresponds to the melting process, that is, solid phase and liquid phase equilibrium. The temperature of this plateau read from the graph is 150 K. Therefore, the temperature at which Substance A is in equilibrium with the liquid phase is 150 K.

Since the first flat segment after heating a solid is melting, the solid phase is in equilibrium with the liquid phase at that plateau. Read its temperature from the y-axis: 150 K.
